name: Chicken (bantam)
notes: Turn eggs at least 5 times a day, an odd number so they do not rest on the same side each night, or use an automatic turner, until the lockdown day. Figures are typical starting points from extension incubation tables (Mississippi State, Texas A&M). Adjust humidity by checking air cell size or weight loss. Still-air temperatures are measured at the top of the eggs, because still-air incubators have warmer and cooler layers; Mississippi State says to add 2 to 3 F to the forced-air setting. No extension table lists bantams separately; they use the chicken settings. Bantam eggs are smaller and keepers often see them hatch a day or so earlier than large fowl, so many lock down on day 17 or 18. That earlier hatch is keeper experience, not an extension figure.

name: Chicken (large fowl)
notes: Turn eggs at least 5 times a day, an odd number so they do not rest on the same side each night, or use an automatic turner, until the lockdown day. Figures are typical starting points from extension incubation tables (Mississippi State, Texas A&M). Adjust humidity by checking air cell size or weight loss. Still-air temperatures are measured at the top of the eggs, because still-air incubators have warmer and cooler layers; Mississippi State says to add 2 to 3 F to the forced-air setting. Some keepers with small forced-air incubators run lower humidity (about 45 to 50%) or dry hatch in humid climates; check the air cell and adjust. Cool or old eggs may hatch a day late.

name: Quail (Coturnix)
notes: Turn eggs at least 5 times a day, an odd number so they do not rest on the same side each night, or use an automatic turner, until the lockdown day. Figures are typical starting points from extension incubation tables (Mississippi State, Texas A&M). Adjust humidity by checking air cell size or weight loss. Still-air temperatures are measured at the top of the eggs, because still-air incubators have warmer and cooler layers; Mississippi State says to add 2 to 3 F to the forced-air setting. name: Goose
notes: Turn eggs at least 5 times a day, an odd number so they do not rest on the same side each night, or use an automatic turner, until the lockdown day. Figures are typical starting points from extension incubation tables (Mississippi State, Texas A&M). Adjust humidity by checking air cell size or weight loss. Still-air temperatures are measured at the top of the eggs, because still-air incubators have warmer and cooler layers; Mississippi State says to add 2 to 3 F to the forced-air setting. Length varies by breed: Mississippi State gives 28 to 34 days and Texas A&M 30 days for domestic geese. Goose eggs need more humidity than chicken eggs and are often cooled and misted daily. Texas A&M moves eggs to the hatcher on day 27, while Mississippi State stops turning after day 25; lock down about 3 days before the expected hatch.
